meta.description: Estimate causal effects of an exposure on an outcome from GWAS summary statistics using genetic instruments. Implements IVW (fixed/random), MR-Egger, weighted median/mode, MR-RAPS, CAUSE, GSMR-HEIDI, MR-PRESSO, MVMR, MR-Clust, LCV, and LHC-MR via TwoSampleMR, MendelianRandomization, MR-PRESSO, cause, and lhcMR. Use when testing causal direction between traits, evaluating drug-target effects via cis-pQTL/cis-eQTL, performing multivariable mediation MR, distinguishing causation from correlated horizontal pleiotropy, or producing STROBE-MR-compliant sensitivity batteries.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI/PMID/trial results/p-values found across any of the 7 outputs. All ~40 references in SKILL.md (Davey Smith 2003, Bowden 2015/2016, Zhao 2020, Morrison 2020, Verbanck 2018, Sanderson 2019/2021, Skrivankova 2021, etc.) are real, correctly-attributed MR literature. Every statistic reported in this audit is a value this session actually computed against real (GIANT BMI15 x PGC MDD18) or clearly-labelled synthetic data with planted ground truth.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 6 (personal-genotype 'should I lose weight for my mental health' framing) was correctly declined, citing SKILL.md's own Decision Tree row ('Single-patient rare disease -> Not MR -- n=1 is wrong regime') and its binary-outcome non-collapsibility caveat against implying an individual intervention effect. Unlike the sibling pleiotropy-detection Skill (audited separately, found to have zero boundary scaffolding), this Skill's own text already carries genuine escape-hatch language.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled methodological fallacy found (no correlation-as-causation substitution, no inverted conclusions). Input 7 found a real imprecision -- the Decision Tree's 'One-sample' row names MR-RAPS as the primary fix, but MR-RAPS empirically failed to correct a planted-zero-effect sample-overlap confound (mean F=44.6, not weak) -- but SKILL.md's own 'Operational rule' and MRlap section elsewhere correctly identify sample-overlap correction as the real remedy, so this is a completeness/cross-referencing gap (captured as a P1), not an inverted or fabricated causal claim.

code_usability.detail: examples/two_sample_mr.R's own shipped MR-PRESSO reporting line, `signif(presso$'MR-PRESSO results'$'Global Test'$Pvalue, 3)`, crashes with 'non-numeric argument to mathematical function' when run verbatim on real, appropriately-pleiotropic GWAS data (GIANT BMI15 x PGC MDD18, 95 harmonised SNPs; Cochran Q p~1e-10) -- reproduced twice (Input 1's full run and an isolated diagnostic, run/mrpresso_pvalue_type_check.R). Root cause confirmed directly from MRPRESSO's own installed source (run/mrpresso_src_check.R): `GlobalTest$Pvalue <- ifelse(GlobalTest$Pvalue == 0, paste0('<', 1/NbDistribution), GlobalTest$Pvalue)` silently converts the field from numeric to a character string whenever the empirical bootstrap p rounds to exactly 0 -- precisely what happens on a real trait pair with strong genuine heterogeneity, which is the flagship use case MR-PRESSO exists to serve. This is the Skill's own central MR-PRESSO Outlier Detection workflow, not a peripheral path.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness and appropriateness excellent (4/4 each) -- taxonomy table, decision tree, per-method failure modes, cis-MR, MVMR, bidirectional, non-linear, cohort gotchas, reviewer pushback, STROBE-MR all covered. Correctness docked to 2/4 for a confirmed, reproducible crash in the Skill's own shipped MR-PRESSO example on real data (see research_veto.code_usability).

reliability.note: Fault Tolerance and Error Reporting both docked (2/4 each): the extensive Common Errors table covers several MR-PRESSO failure modes ('returns NA p-value', 'not enough instrumental variables') but not the capped-Pvalue-becomes-character crash actually found, and the crash itself surfaces as a raw, unexplained R error rather than an actionable message. Recoverability 3/4 -- most other failure modes have clear documented remedies (switch to qhet_mvmr, MR-RAPS, colocalization redirect).

performance_context.note: Efficient decision-tree gating (only escalate to CAUSE/LHC-MR/qhet_mvmr when the regime requires it), but usage-guide.md duplicates rather than layers SKILL.md's Decision Tree, thresholds, and Tips content, and SKILL.md itself has no references/ folder despite very high reference-table density.

agent_usability.note: Very clear vocabulary and explicit output specs at every step (Learnability 4, Consistency 4). Feedback Design and Error Prevention both docked to 2/4: the shipped example's own cat()-based reporting silently breaks exactly at the MR-PRESSO summary line, and neither the SIMEX-crash footgun nor the coloc-demo data-generation mismatch found in this audit are anticipated anywhere in the text.

human_usability.note: Precise, domain-correct trigger language matching how researchers actually phrase MR requests (drug-target, MVMR, STROBE-MR, causal direction). Graceful handling across most of the tested input range; docked 1 point for the Steiger-needs-samplesize_col trap that silently returns NULL rather than erroring when SKILL.md's own inline 'Bidirectional and Steiger' code block is followed verbatim (it never sets samplesize either).

security.note: No credential or data-safety issues; JWT-token requirement for OpenGWAS is documented accurately and specifically. No defensive input-validation layer of its own beyond what TwoSampleMR/MRPRESSO/MVMR provide, and this audit found that reliance can fail (MR-PRESSO's own type-changing Pvalue field).

maintainability.note: Clean modular split (SKILL.md / usage-guide.md / examples/), but SKILL.md and usage-guide.md duplicate the Decision Tree, thresholds and Tips content near-verbatim -- the same authoring pattern found in the sibling pleiotropy-detection Skill in this folder. Testability docked (2/4): the shipped example scripts run on their own synthetic toy data without ever exercising the exact real-data condition (a capped MR-PRESSO p-value) that breaks them.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger description and an excellent Related-Skills composability map (colocalization-analysis, mediation-analysis, pleiotropy-detection, proteome-mr-drug-target, fine-mapping). Progressive Disclosure docked to 2/4: SKILL.md is ~410 lines of dense reference tables with no references/ folder at all. Idempotency 3/4 and Escape Hatches 4/4 (the n=1 'Not MR' row and one-sample operational rule are genuine, well-designed, and confirmed working by execution).

key_strengths: The real-data run (GIANT BMI15 x PGC MDD18, 95 harmonised SNPs) exactly reproduced the IVW/Egger/weighted-median/weighted-mode point estimates independently verified in this candidate's own TOOLS.md smoke test, and additionally produced a working Steiger directionality result once SKILL.md's own documented samplesize_col fields were supplied.

Unlike the sibling pleiotropy-detection Skill (audited separately), this Skill's own text already contains real practice-boundary scaffolding -- the explicit 'n=1 is wrong regime -> not MR' decision-tree row and the binary-outcome non-collapsibility caveat -- and Input 6 confirmed the Skill correctly declines and redirects a personal-health framing using that language.

MVMR branching logic (conditional F -> qhet_mvmr fallback) was validated end to end against planted ground truth: both the primary IVW-MVMR and the low-conditional-F fallback estimator recovered the true direct effects closely.

cis-MR and sparse-instrument point estimates were highly accurate against planted ground truth across both a well-powered 25-SNP regime (Input 2) and an extreme 3-SNP edge case (Input 3), and MR-PRESSO's documented 'not enough instrumental variables' failure mode was reproduced with the exact same error string found independently in the sibling audit.

recommendations.title: Shipped MR-PRESSO reporting code crashes on real, strongly-pleiotropic GWAS data
recommendations.problem: examples/two_sample_mr.R's own `signif(presso$'MR-PRESSO results'$'Global Test'$Pvalue, 3)` line crashes with 'non-numeric argument to mathematical function' when run verbatim on real GIANT-BMI x PGC-MDD data (95 SNPs) -- reproduced twice.
recommendations.root_cause: MRPRESSO's own source silently converts GlobalTest$Pvalue from numeric to a capped character string (e.g. '<0.0002') whenever the empirical bootstrap p rounds to exactly 0 (`GlobalTest$Pvalue <- ifelse(GlobalTest$Pvalue == 0, paste0('<', 1/NbDistribution), GlobalTest$Pvalue)`), which is exactly what happens on a real trait pair with strong genuine heterogeneity -- the flagship use case for MR-PRESSO.
recommendations.fix: Guard every place Global Test / Distortion Test / Outlier Test Pvalue fields are formatted, e.g. `gt_p <- presso$'MR-PRESSO results'$'Global Test'$Pvalue; cat('p:', if (is.numeric(gt_p)) signif(gt_p, 3) else gt_p)`. Apply in examples/two_sample_mr.R and any inline SKILL.md MR-PRESSO snippet using the same pattern.

recommendations.title: Decision Tree overstates MR-RAPS as the fix for one-sample-equivalent designs
recommendations.problem: MR-RAPS reproduced essentially the same significant bias as naive IVW (b=0.196 vs 0.180, both far from the planted true effect of 0) in a UKB-on-UKB simulation with a strong mean F-statistic (44.6), because the actual bias source was sample-overlap/confounding, not weak instruments.
recommendations.root_cause: The Decision Tree table's 'One-sample' row lists only 'IVW with weak-IV-aware (MR-RAPS)' as the primary method, without cross-referencing the file's own correct Burgess 2016 / MRlap sample-overlap correction that appears later in the same document.
recommendations.fix: Edit the Decision Tree row to read 'IVW with sample-overlap correction (Burgess 2016 / MRlap); MR-RAPS only if instruments are ALSO weak (F<20)' so the table itself does not imply MR-RAPS alone is sufficient.

recommendations.title: SIMEX correction is prose-only with no code, and the natural way to write it crashes
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md instructs 'SIMEX-correct via the simex package applied to the Egger fit, treating se.exposure as measurement error' but gives no code block; the natural R pattern (weights = 1/se.outcome^2 as a bare in-formula column reference) reproducibly crashes inside simex()'s internal refit with 'object se.outcome not found'.
recommendations.root_cause: simex() cannot resolve bare column names via non-standard evaluation outside the original calling data frame at refit time, and nothing in SKILL.md warns of this.
recommendations.fix: Add a working inline code pattern: precompute `w <- 1 / dat$se.outcome^2` before `lm(beta.outcome ~ beta.exposure, weights = w, data = dat, x = TRUE, y = TRUE)`, then pass the fitted model to simex() unchanged.

recommendations.title: cis-MR/coloc example's synthetic data cannot demonstrate its own claimed PP.H4 >= 0.7 threshold
recommendations.problem: Running examples/cis_mr_drug_target.R's exact data-generating pattern (independent per-SNP simulated effects, no real LD structure) on a genuinely single-shared-causal-variant ground truth still returned PP.H4=0.197, well below the 'DRUG-TARGET SUPPORTED' threshold the example's own comment implies.
recommendations.root_cause: coloc.abf's Bayesian model assumes LD-linked, single-causal-variant-per-locus association patterns; generating each SNP's effect independently (as both the shipped example and this audit's ground-truth replication do) does not produce that pattern regardless of the true underlying biology.
recommendations.fix: Either simulate the cis-window with real LD-decayed effects (draw one causal SNP effect and propagate to neighbors via an LD matrix) or add a caveat in the example/SKILL.md that the demo's PP.H4 is illustrative-only and not expected to reliably clear 0.7.

recommendations.title: No seed set before Monte-Carlo MR-PRESSO calls in SKILL.md's own inline code block
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's 'MR-PRESSO Outlier Detection' inline code block never calls set.seed() before mr_presso(), whose global test is a randomized permutation procedure.
recommendations.root_cause: Reproducibility guidance was written into the examples' data-simulation seed but not carried into the MR-PRESSO call itself.
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit set.seed() call immediately before the mr_presso() call in SKILL.md's inline code block, with a one-line note on why (Monte-Carlo global test).

recommendations.title: SKILL.md and usage-guide.md duplicate content instead of layering it
recommendations.problem: The Decision Tree, Quantitative Thresholds, and Tips content appear near-verbatim in both SKILL.md and usage-guide.md -- the same authoring pattern independently found in the sibling pleiotropy-detection Skill in this folder -- so a fix (such as the P0 above) needs applying consistently across both, and the duplication adds token cost without adding depth.
recommendations.root_cause: No references/ folder exists to hold shared reference tables; usage-guide.md was written as a second full pass rather than a thinner example-prompt layer.
recommendations.fix: Move shared tabular reference content (Decision Tree, Quantitative Thresholds, Cohort Gotchas) into a references/ file that both SKILL.md and usage-guide.md point to, rather than duplicating it.
